ADOPTED.licensed_for: post-freeze surfaces: Phase-2 fits, daily refits, Phase-4 grids
ADOPTED.not_licensed_for: the frozen candidate, which was and stays stdlib-fitted

NOT_ADOPTED_AND_NOT_DELIVERED.columnar_cache: NOT BUILT by this run and its benefit is UNVERIFIED
NOT_ADOPTED_AND_NOT_DELIVERED.consequence: the '0.04s parse' benefit does NOT follow from this gate. Wiring the cache into the row-loading path is separate work needing its own gate.
NOT_ADOPTED_AND_NOT_DELIVERED.measured_instead: 4.0x overall (4525s -> 1141s). The ~226x applies to the fits; parse+features are unchanged and are now the dominant cost.
NOT_ADOPTED_AND_NOT_DELIVERED.why: all seven swapped functions are FIT functions; none touches row loading, so save_columnar/load_columnar were never invoked. run_fine still json.loads the 1.24 GB file.

authority: R-167(b) / R-155(2): adoption licensed only by ONE full-scale reproduction to the cent
honest_note: The speedup is real and large but it is 4x, not 226x, at the level that matters to a Phase-2 run. Quoting 226x for end-to-end work would overstate it by ~56x.

structural_checks.why_these_matter: a gate that silently fell back to the stdlib path would reproduce the targets perfectly and prove nothing; the identity assertion makes that a raise, not a quiet pass
